seen_animation: Frames 1-8: a line-drawn shovel lies still across the frame, handle running from a small triangular grip at left to a five-sided blade at right, with grey grass and twig marks as scenery. Frame 9: a black-outlined foot and lower leg enter from the top right, above the blade. Frame 10: that foot is set down on the ground just left of the blade. Frame 11: a second foot appears at the top right edge, partly cut off by the frame. Frame 12: the second leg comes down beside the blade while a shoe is lifted at the upper left. Frames 13-14: two feet stand on the ground to the left of the blade, then shift slightly. Frame 15: a hand with squared fingers appears at the top left beside the legs. Frame 16: the arm reaches down between the legs and the hand comes to the shovel handle near the grip.
seen_film: Frames 1-8: a real shovel lies still on dry straw-covered ground, handle at left, blade at right. Frame 9: a foot in grey trousers steps in from the top right above the blade. Frame 10: the foot lands next to the blade. Frame 11: the second foot appears at the top right. Frame 12: the person steps over, one foot planted by the blade and the other lifted at the upper left. Frames 13-14: both feet stand left of the blade. Frame 15: a hand comes down at the top left beside the legs. Frame 16: the person bends and the hand reaches down to grab the shovel handle.
named_subject: A shovel lying on the ground, approached by a person whose feet, legs and hand enter to pick it up.
evidence: Frames 1-8 hold the shovel still, as the film does. In frame 9 the foot enters top right above the blade, matching film frame 9; in frame 10 it is planted just left of the blade, matching film frame 10; frame 11 has the second foot at the top right edge as in the film; frame 12 has one foot lifted upper left and one leg by the blade as in film 12; frames 13-14 place the two feet at the same left and center positions as the film; frame 15 brings the hand in at the top left and frame 16 brings it down to the handle at about the same x position as film frame 16. The shovel keeps the doodle's triangular grip, single thin shaft line and angular blade with a tick at the collar in every frame. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: In frames 15-16 the hand is drawn as a rectangle with square comb-like fingers, and in frame 16 the arm lines sit on top of the leg lines so the lower legs, arm and hand read as a stack of five near-parallel verticals that is hard to separate.
closes_when: Frame 16 shows the arm clearly as one bent limb coming down in front of the legs with its own angle, ending in a hand drawn with the same few loose straight strokes as the shovel rather than a squared comb.
protect: The still shovel in frames 1-8 that keeps the doodle's construction; the timing of each foot entry and step (frames 9-14) at the same frame positions as the film; the hand arriving at frame 15 and reaching the handle at frame 16; the sparse thin-line style with unchanged grey scenery.
identity_gap: The shovel is the doodle's drawing (triangle grip, thin shaft, angular blade), but the added hand uses a squared comb shape that does not match the doodle's loose stroke habits.
